items.title: Weighing 600 million buildings reveals global urban material inequality and efficiency paths
items.display_title: Weighing 600 million buildings reveals global urban material inequality and efficiency paths
items.summary: Urbanization is rapidly increasing the accumulation of materials in buildings worldwide. This study’s global mapping of over 600 million buildings reveals that urban form, alongside affluence, critically shapes patterns of material stock growth.

items.title: Topographic accessibility and proto-urban settlement organization in Neolithic China
items.display_title: Topographic accessibility and proto-urban settlement organization in Neolithic China
items.summary: The origins of modern cities can be found in proto-urban settlements that formed before the consolidation of states. This study demonstrates that spatial terrain accessibility guided settlement organization in Neolithic China, a relationship that can be tested in other contexts.
